selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: H.R. 10578, the AI DATA Act, directs federal agencies to collect and publish new labor market data. The law focuses specifically on measuring how artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies affect jobs, hiring, worker training, and labor force participation.

affected_groups.effect: Workers will be surveyed through household and longitudinal studies to track employment outcomes, earnings, and how time allocation changes due to artificial intelligence.
Employers will participate in monthly establishment surveys and the Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey regarding technology adoption, hiring, and separations.
Agencies are tasked with designing surveys, integrating multi-source data, publishing monthly, quarterly, and annual metrics, and producing reports on artificial intelligence workforce impacts.
affected_groups.group: Federal Agencies (Department of Labor, Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census)

key_provisions: Requires the Secretary of Labor to conduct a monthly recurring survey of businesses regarding job openings, hiring, and worker separations, grouped by industry, occupation, and location to assess technological changes.
Requires a recurring household survey to measure how individuals spend time across work, caregiving, education, and other activities, including questions on digital tools and emerging technologies.
Requires longitudinal surveys following individuals over extended periods to track employment, earnings, mobility, and the long-term effects of artificial intelligence.

Authorizes specific funding appropriations for fiscal year 2027 and the next five years for these new labor data collections ($8 million annually for labor market flow data, $5 million annually for time-use data, and $20 million annually for longitudinal data).
Directs the Director of the Census, in coordination with other officials, to incorporate artificial intelligence questions into the Business Trends and Outlook Survey and publish quarterly results.
Requires the Secretary of Labor and the Secretary of Commerce to publish an annual joint report integrating various federal data sources to assess how artificial intelligence impacts the workforce.
Establishes a 10-year sunset for the Business Trends and Outlook Survey additions and the joint agency reporting requirements.
missing_information: The text does not specify exact total funding sums for sections 5 and 6, stating only such sums as may be necessary.
The source does not mention enforcement mechanisms or penalties for businesses that fail to complete the required surveys.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 10578, the AI DATA Act, directs federal agencies to collect and publish new labor market data. The law focuses specifically on measuring how artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies affect jobs, hiring, worker training, and labor force participation.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes an ongoing federal data collection and reporting framework dedicated to measuring the economic and workforce changes driven by artificial intelligence. By committing millions in new authorizations over multiple years, it aims to provide policymakers and the public with regular metrics on technological shifts in the labor market.
